headlines.title: Crash in San Jose leaves bicyclist with life-threatening injuries
headlines.description: A cyclist suffered life-threatening injuries in a crash in San Jose on Thursday night, according to the police department. Authorities said the crash was reported at 7:24 p.m. in the area of Altamara Avenue and Moncucco Way. According to police, the bicyclist was taken to a local hospital while the driver involved remained on the scene. Police said Altamara Avenue from Pinotin Court to Eldiva Court will be blocked off for a significant amount of time. Officials advised the public to drive with caution and use alternate routes.

headlines.title: 2 active tuberculosis cases linked to San Francisco strip club, officials say
headlines.description: Thursday, the San Francisco Department of Public Health confirmed it is looking into two active cases of tuberculosis “associated with The Crazy Horse establishment in San Francisco.” The Crazy Horse is a strip club on Market Street that’s been in existence for more than three decades. The department told NBC Bay Area that it was notified of the first confirmed case in early October, and then began contact tracing efforts to identify people who may have been exposed. “These efforts are ongoing and at this time, the risk to the general public is low,” the department said in a statement. “If this status changes, we will let the public know.” Tuberculosis (or TB) is an infectious disease caused by bacteria. To contract it, health experts say, you will need to have prolonged exposure to a contagious person. Dr. Abraar Karan, who is a member of the Infectious Diseases faculty at Stanford, explained that the bacteria that cause tuberculosis are airborne. “The bacteria can hang around in the air long after someone is no longer in that space,” Karan added. “Spaces that are crowded with poor ventilation or where you have very close contact with someone that is contagious are going to be higher risk for transmission,” explained Karan explained that there are two types of tuberculosis: active and latent. Most people who contract tuberculosis get latent tuberculosis and do not show symptoms, and are not immediately contagious. However, over time and without treatment, that person can develop active tuberculosis, which is contagious and a serious illness. The symptoms of active tuberculosis can include fever, coughing, weight loss, and night sweats, Karan noted. Dr. Peter Chin-Hong, a Professor of Medicine and Infectious Disease Specialist at UCSF, believes the SFDPH contact tracing teams will be tracking these cases for a while because the bacteria that causes tuberculosis grows very slowly. “They’ll do testing and probably repeat the testing in a few weeks, because again, sometimes the testing may be negative, but because [the bacteria] grows so slowly, eventually that test may turn positive if there was a true infection,” he noted. Chin-Hong also cautioned: these two cases don’t automatically mean there is an outbreak. “[Public Health officials] have to establish at least two cases that are linked, and we’re not even sure at this point whether the two cases are actually acquired at the establishment, or they got it somewhere else,” Chin-Hong said. He noted that the San Francisco Department of Health will be assessing who is most at risk and contacting them. The San Francisco Department of Public Health said it is important for people at risk of tuberculosis to get tested and treated. NBC Bay Area reached out to Crazy Horse for comment, but has not received a response.

headlines.title: Marin County Search and Rescue volunteers recount days-long Mount Shasta rescue
headlines.description: A wrong turn on the way down Mount Shasta left a climber with a severely injured leg, stranded more than 12,000 feet up over the weekend. For nearly three days, rescuers battled high winds, treacherous terrain and dangerous weather to get him off the mountain. Three Marin County Search and Rescue volunteers say they were racing against time, climbing through rockfall and high winds to reach a man who was badly hurt. They say getting him off the mountain would prove to be just as dangerous. “This was certainly a challenge, a challenging rescue, one of the most challenging I’ve been on,” rescuer Nick Slaneck said. The 39-year-old Florida man had summited Mount Shasta Sunday, but on the way down, he followed the wrong GPS route. Then, a snow bridge gave way. He fell through, severely hurting his leg, about 12,000 feet up the mountain. He had running shoes, a sweatshirt and no easy way down, so he called 911. U.S. Forest Service rangers reached him on Monday, but dangerous weather kept rescuers from getting him out. By Tuesday, the push to bring him down was on. “It took us a number of hours to get up there because of the difficulty of terrain,” rescuer Jayne Wolk said. When rescuers finally reached him, the man was still talking, but the cold was taking its toll. “He was coherent and talking to us, but he was certainly cold,” Slaneck said. Then, a break in the weather. A CHP helicopter got the opening it needed, but reaching the climber was only half the battle. Rescuers still had to get him into the aircraft on a mountain where one wrong move could make a bad situation even worse. “There was a moment where we were just like, ‘Alright one, two, three,’ lifted his head up and just got it over, the folded up backseat of the helicopter, fit it and just took out hands off and stepped away and at that moment where we’re like ‘He’s in, we’re done’,” rescuer Nathan Fisher said. After hours of climbing, fighting the elements, and working to get the man to safety, he was finally on board. “That moment, when we all got him on the helicopter and we knew the mission was accomplished, at least on our end, there was a huge verbal sigh of relief that everybody gave and everybody was hugging each other and everybody took a knee and got really centered in that moment,” Slaneck said. For the rescuers, that was the moment the tension finally broke. The climber was airlifted to a hospital Tuesday night, bringing a nearly three-day rescue to an end. And while the helicopter got him off the mountain, rescuers say it took a number of agencies working together to get him there. “It was just really a group effort and every member of the team and everyone there had something to contribute,” Wolk said. A rescue that demanded hours of grit, a narrow window of opportunity, and a team that kept going until the climber was safe.

headlines.title: Community advocates concerned after ICE agents spotted at Milpitas jail
headlines.description: Community advocates raised concerns about ICE activity at a South Bay jail. Cellphone video obtained by NBC Bay Area shows armed federal immigration agents both inside and outside the Elmwood Correctional Facility in Milpitas. Advocates with Silicon Valley De-Bug and the Santa Clara County Rapid Response Network were at the facility, raising questions about why agents were there and whether their activity conflicts with the county’s sanctuary policy. “It is deeply concerning. This feels like a recent escalation, and we don’t know if it’s the beginning of a larger operation or what’s motivating it,” Raj Jayadev with Silicon Valley De-Bug said. “They were here yesterday so we were ready, Rapid Response Network was out here as well.” Raj Jayadev says both Silicon Valley De-Bug and the Rapid Response Network are concerned that the agents are waiting to pick up people, just as they’re being released. “We had seen people and known people that were being released from jail and they never made it home because ICE was waiting for them to pick them up,” Jayadev said. The sheriff’s office says the agents did not make any arrests or detainments Thursday and remained in areas open to the public. Advocates say they believe ICE’s presence conflicts with the county’s civil immigration policy, which generally prohibits county staff from helping with federal civil immigration enforcement, including sharing release dates. “I think our concerns are to make sure the sheriffs in the county are not participating in anything that ICE wants to do,” Narely Campos with Silicon Valley De-Bug said. It’s worth noting that no sanctuary policy can prohibit the agents from waiting inside or outside public areas of the jail. In a statement, the sheriff’s office reiterated that it does not coordinate with ICE, notify the agency of release dates or have advance knowledge of its operations. The office says ICE has periodically visited the jail’s lobby for more than a year and has taken 60 people into custody who were scheduled for release. The sheriff’s office says there were no incidents reported and jail operations continued as normal.

headlines.title: San Francisco house allegedly occupied by squatters to go up for auction
headlines.description: In one of San Francisco’s most exclusive neighborhoods, a house that neighbors claim is occupied by squatters will go up for auction soon. The four-bedroom house on 32nd Avenue in the Sea Cliff neighborhood seems to fit right in on the upscale street, but neighbors say squatters have been a persistent problem. “It’s quiet right now in the middle of the day when they’re not here, but if you came between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m., you’d be hearing dogs barking all night, car doors slamming,” resident Cameron Will said. “There were enormous thuds last night keeping neighbors up. That’s very common. I’d say that’s probably five out of seven days a week.” Will said the ongoing nuisance has resulted in neighbors resorting to documenting everyone who comes and goes. Will said they’ve counted up to three dozen people over the last two months. No one answered the door when an NBC Bay Area crew knocked Thursday. The San Francisco Board of Supervisors this week authorized the city to put the house on auction due to years of unpaid property taxes that now total about $340,000. The city attorney also has filed a lawsuit against Diana Peng, Brandon Aadee and several unnamed people, alleging Peng and Aadee are conspiring to illegally gain title of the house. The special auction will likely be set for December. According to online real estate estimates, it could be worth upwards of $4 million. But if someone produces a valid title and is able to pay the tax bill, the whole plan could be derailed, along with neighbors’ hopes of finding some peace on their street.

headlines.title: Popular Safeway in San Jose to close
headlines.description: A popular Safeway store in San Jose is closing, and for some customers, it’s the end of an era. A sign posted outside the Safeway store on Bollinger Road in the Orchard Farms Shopping Center says the store will shut its doors on Nov. 13. Some neighbors say they’ve been shopping here for decades and will miss more than just the convenience. “I sent them a message, I hope they renew it, because these are lifetime memories here. Raised 2 of my daughters, oldest is 48,” San Jose resident Shayesteh Ahmed said. Others say the closure will leave a gap especially for people who shop off-hours. The Chronicle reports Safeway has closed stores in San Francisco, Pinole, Vallejo and Hayward over the past two years. NBC Bay Area reached out to Safeway’s parent company, Albertsons, about the closure but has not heard back.

headlines.title: How a dual language program is helping a struggling San Jose school district
headlines.description: A San Jose school district is considering reopening a campus it previously closed thanks to a successful dual language immersion program. Declining enrollment has school districts across California, including San Jose’s Alum Rock Union Elementary School District (ARUSD), facing the prospect of closing schools. ARUSD’s Ben Painter Elementary School was on the list of schools slated to potentially close due to low enrollment, but demand for its Vietnamese dual language immersion program ballooned this fall. “This year we have every classroom full,” Painter Elementary Principal Dr. Joseph Manluco said. “We have kids in every classroom with a large and growing Vietnamese dual language immersion program.” There are 420 students at Painter Elementary, a number that might bode well for other campuses that are currently shut down. “We do have other campuses within the district that are exceeding enrollment, where they need more room,” ARUSD Superintendent Dr. Marnie Hazelton said. “We are working with committees along with our board members and a local real estate agency to see if it is a viable option to reopen some of these campuses.” Pew Research estimates San Jose has the largest population of Vietnamese people outside of Vietnam at roughly 150,000. Painter Elementary’s program is the second largest Vietnamese dual language immersion program in Northern California. The idea is to combine quality academics with a second language. But there are plenty of non-Vietnamese American students on campus. “We have students in here that are becoming trilingual or even quadrilingual,” Manluco said.

headlines.title: WNBA Finals: Valks look to even series vs. Dream after dropping back-to-back games
headlines.description: The Golden State Valkyries will look to stop the surging Atlanta Dream in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals. A win for the Valks at Saturday’s game in Atlanta would even the best-of-seven series at 2-2. A loss would put Golden State on the brink of elimination and give Atlanta its first title. Game 4 comes after the Dream won back-to-back games against the Valkyries, who won the series opener. How to watch Valkyries vs. Dream in the WNBA Finals The series will air across NBC and USA Network. Game 4 will be on NBC Bay Area. All games can also be streamed on Peacock. Where to stream Valkyries vs. Dream WNBA Finals games live online In addition to Peacock, there are other platforms where the Finals can be streamed. headlines.title: Highway 37 in North Bay to close this weekend for El Niño storm preps
headlines.description: Highway 37 in the North Bay will shut down in both directions this weekend to allow Caltrans crews time to raise the flood-prone area ahead of a potentially powerful El Niño and winter storms. Motorists traveling through the area should expect significant delays and increased travel times. Here’s what to know about the closure and detour information. When will Highway 37 shut down? The closure on the highway starts at 10 p.m. Friday. Caltrans expects to reopen lanes by 5 a.m. Monday. What part of Highway 37 will close during weekend closure? Highway 37 will shut down between Mare Island in Vallejo and Sears Point in Sonoma County, according to Caltrans. Detour information for Highway 37 closure Motorists traveling on eastbound Highway 37 during the closure will exit left onto northbound Highway 121 in Sonoma; Make a right on Highway 12, 1(Carneros Hwy) and continue; Right on Highway 12/Highway 29; Enter left for the connector loop off-ramp back to eastbound Highway 37. Motorists traveling on westbound Highway 37 will exit right onto northbound Highway 29 in Napa, and follow Highway 29 to westbound Highway 12, then to southbound Highway 121; Why is Caltrans shutting down Highway 37? Highway 37 near Mare Island has flooded repeatedly over the years. Caltrans said the work is designed to help reduce flooding risks on the vital commuter route. headlines.title: Pacifica Pier repairs cause traffic headaches
headlines.description: Major repairs at the Pacifica Pier are causing traffic headaches for people in the area. A large crane and other heavy equipment have rolled in along Beach Boulevard Thursday, which will be used to stabilize the cracked pier. “Right now there is a void there and wave will continue to wash away, and we want to make sure we protect the street and the utilities and the residences in the neighborhood,” Pacifica City Manager Sean Charpentier said. It could take crews up to five days to position the crane, while the overall repair phase is expected to last at least three months. The pier has been closed since June, when engineers discovered major cracking. The city says it’s moving as quickly as possible to create this “temporary fix” due to the expected record-breaking storm season. “So, this does not fix the pier, this just helps to shore it up to protect it though the winter,” Charpentier said. Residents are being warned to expect noise, and the city says parking could temporarily be affected. The city also says it’s still evaluating longer term repair options.

headlines.title: World's top squash players compete in Redwood City
headlines.description: Some of the world’s top squash players were competing in Redwood City on Thursday. Squash is a fast-paced racket sport making its Olympic debut at the 2028 games in LA. It’s played by two singles or four players in sets of doubles on an enclosed four-walled court with a small, using a hollow rubber ball. The quarterfinals at the “Silicon Valley Open”, a pro squash tournament, were held on Thursday. 48 of the world’s top squash players are competing for a $260,000 grand prize. The finals are on Saturday.

headlines.title: Preliminary 3.0 magnitude earthquake strikes near Hollister
headlines.description: A preliminary 3.0 magnitude earthquake struck near Hollister, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 2:58 p.m. and was centered 14.6 miles south-southeast of Hollister, the USGS said. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.
